This raises serious question marks regarding the democratic embedding and the oversight of the execution of the activities.
Dat roept grote vraagtekens op wat betreft de democratische inbedding en het toezicht op de uitvoering van de werkzaamheden.
Worries that greater distance from democratically elected bodies weakens democratic control and asks how volunteer participation and medezeggenschap are secured.
These members note, however, that this increases the distance to a democratically elected body and are therefore not yet convinced that this is the right organisational form.
Deze leden constateren echter dat hiermee de afstand tot een democratisch gekozen orgaan groter wordt en zijn daarom nog niet overtuigd dat dit de juiste organisatievorm is.
Doubts the abolition of municipal fire brigades given the large volunteer commitment and asks how local anchoring and local steering are preserved.
The SGP members are not yet convinced in advance that it is good to remove the possibility of a municipal fire brigade from the law.
De leden van de SGP-fractie zijn er nog niet op voorhand van overtuigd dat het goed is om de mogelijkheid voor een gemeentelijke brandweer uit de wet te halen.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advised revising the bill that fully regionalises fire services and creates the Instituut Fysieke Veiligheid, mainly on the coherence with police reform, fire-service training responsibilities, the vagueness between statutory and common tasks, and redactional points. The minister's reply accepted the task-allocation and redaction points and the clarification on the regionalisation but declined to make IFV responsible for training and to include a statutory evaluation obligation.
concerns: The Afdeling asked the explanation to address the coherence between full regionalisation of fire services and police scale-up; the government added to the explanatory memorandum but disputed the claim about the mayor's difficulty with volunteer policy.

The Afdeling advised placing the statutory training-system tasks with the IFV under ministerial responsibility including financial; the government declined, pointing to the employers' responsibility and the ongoing study.
The Afdeling found the boundary between statutory and common tasks of the IFV unclear, given separate cost registration; the bill was amended to distinguish tasks from activities.
The Afdeling advised not weakening the statutory obligation to set rules on training; the government argued the bill tightens rather than weakens the competence requirements.

The Afdeling advised a statutory evaluation provision because cooperation from bodies outside ministerial responsibility is needed; the government considered a statutory duty unnecessary and undesirable.
The Afdeling advised adding that the IFV confidentiality clause does not affect the minister's duty to inform parliament under Article 68 of the Constitution; this was added.
The Afdeling gave a list of redactional comments; most were adopted, but the deletion of the second paragraph of Article 74 (insolvency safeguard) was not.

33057.s: The bill consolidates the funding and financial management rules of the financial supervisors AFM and DNB into one Act, replacing sector-specific funding provisions in several supervisory statutes. It sets a fixed state contribution, redistributes supervision costs across supervised categories by fixed percentages, and requires ministerial consent to the supervisors' budgets, annual accounts and reports.
33057.j: The memorandum justifies the consolidated funding rules by reducing fluctuating levies, simplifying legislation and linking the state contribution to the budget, with ministers monitoring costs.
q: No appeal may be lodged against ministerial decisions approving the budget, annual accounts or report, or on settling the operating surplus, under section 8:1 of the General Administrative Law Act.

Tegen besluiten van Onze Ministers inzake instemming met de begroting, de jaarrekening of de verantwoording alsmede tegen besluiten van Onze Ministers omtrent de verrekening van het exploitatiesaldo kan geen beroep worden ingesteld als bedoeld in artikel 8:1 van de Algemene wet bestuursrecht.
d: rules for structuring the supervisor's budget
further rules for the annual report
further rules on fee reductions for one-off supervisory acts
fee bandwidths and tariffs per supervisory category
p: Ministers jointly approve supervisors' budgets and may decide to exclude part of an operating surplus from fee calculation, shifting cost-setting discretion to the executive while the regulated sector bears costs.

Ministerial decisions on approving budgets, accounts and surplus allocation are excluded from administrative appeal under the General Administrative Law Act, limiting judicial review by affected firms.}

parties: Asks for clarification on the shift of supervisory costs to the financial sector and how cumulative regulation costs will be passed on to clients.
These members assume that all these costs will be passed on to customers.
Deze leden gaan er vanuit dat al deze kosten zullen worden doorberekend aan de klanten.
Asks whether setting levies only once every five years risks surpluses or deficits at the supervisors and how shortfalls would be covered.
The PvdA members ask whether setting the levies only once every five years does not create a risk of surpluses or deficits at the supervisors.
De leden van de PvdA-fractie vragen of het slechts één keer in de vijf jaar vaststellen van de heffingen niet leidt tot het risico dat bij de toezichthouders overschotten dan wel tekorten ontstaan.
Questions whether financing supervision of financial markets from general funds is consistent with the profit principle and the earlier report Maat houden.

The PVV members ask whether the government does not see the ordering of (financial) markets as a typical government task, so that the costs of financial supervision of EUR 200 million should be paid from general funds on that basis.

De leden van de PVV-fractie vragen of de regering de ordening van de (financiële) markten niet als een typische overheidstaak ziet en de kosten voor het financiële toezicht, groot € 200 mln., op die grond dan niet uit de algemene middelen moeten worden voldaan.
Asks about the cost increases for business, whether they coincide with other measures, and the size and volatility of the exploitation balance.
The CDA members ask to what extent these burden increases for business coincide with other measures.
De leden van de CDA-fractie vragen in hoeverre deze lastenstijgingen voor het bedrijfsleven niet samenvallen met andere maatregelen?
Asks for figures on how the fixed government contribution will change through wage and price adjustments and budget cuts, and for ten-year overviews of contributions.
The SP members ask the government to show in figures how the level of the fixed government contribution will change through wage and price adjustments and imposed budget cuts.

De leden van de SP-fractie vragen de regering cijfermatig te laten zien hoe de hoogte van de forfaitaire overheidsbijdrage veranderd gaat worden door loon- en prijsbijstellingen en opgelegde taakstellingen.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised on a bill on financing of financial supervision (AFM and DNB), a fixed state contribution and a ministerial criterion for withholding consent to supervisory budgets; it recommended deleting the provision on further elaboration of the 'public interest' criterion and clarifying the fixed state contribution. The government's reply accepted deletion of the provision, expanded the explanatory memorandum on the fixed contribution and adopted the redactional remarks.
concerns: The Afdeling advised deleting the power for ministers to further define the 'public interest' criterion in advance, as it was not clearly necessary; the government deleted it.

The fixed state contribution breaks the link with actual supervisory costs and the bill does not clearly fix amounts after the first year; the government clarified the memorandum and made annual adjustments explicit in article 10(3), but did not change the fixed nature.
Redactional remarks on the Wet bestuursrechtspraak bedrijfsorganisatie annex, delegation provision, definitions and article 23 were adopted.

33090-V.s: This bill amends the departmental budget statement of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for 2011, shifting appropriations across policy articles in the supplementary budget (Najaarsnota) and setting the amounts in thousands of euros. It takes effect from 1 December of the budget year, with retroactive effect if the Staatsblad is published later.
q: The departmental budget statement of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (V) for the year 2011 is amended, as shown in the state annexed to this law.
Artikel 1 De departementale begrotingsstaat van het Ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken (V) voor het jaar 2011 wordt gewijzigd, zoals blijkt uit de desbetreffende bij deze wet behorende staat.

33129.s: The bill amends the Civil Code and the Rent Price Regulation Act so that an annual rent increase for regulated housing depends on household income. Landlords may obtain a Tax Authority statement indicating whether household income exceeds EUR 43,000 and attach it to the rent increase proposal.
33129.j: The memorandum justifies the ministerial rules by the need to set the maximum increase percentage and the procedure for income statements, and it addresses privacy concerns by limiting the Tax Authority statement to a yes/no indication.
q: Because the Tax Authority statement only indicates whether household income does or does not exceed EUR 43,000, tenants' privacy regarding their income is affected as little as possible.

Doordat de verklaring van de Belastingdienst uitsluitend aangeeft of het huishoudinkomen al dan niet meer bedraagt dan € 43 000, wordt de privacy van huurders waar het gaat om hun inkomen zo min mogelijk aangetast.
d: rules on the income statement procedure
further rules for the Tax Authority income statement
which household income data the tenant must provide
maximum rent increase percentage and income threshold adjustment
p: ARTIKEL I, C (7:252a) and ARTIKEL II, D (Uhw 13)

Tenants' household income data is shared with landlords via a Tax Authority statement, and the rent commission assesses household income in disputes, shifting some protection from the state's data handling toward landlords and the executive's income-based rent regime.
Confidentiality rules limit the use of tax income data by landlords to rent proposals only, with storage and secrecy duties attached.
The minister must report to parliament on effectiveness and practical effects within three years.

parties: Asks how privacy of income data is protected in objection procedures and how disputes with the Belastingdienst are handled.
To what extent is privacy guaranteed in the objection procedure and at the petition stage?
In hoeverre is de privacy in de bezwaarprocedure en in de fase van het verzoekschrift gewaarborgd?
Opposes the bill as one-sided, questions privacy safeguards, and demands that a downward rent adjustment be legally required when income falls.
According to the PvdA members, the privacy element is insufficiently safeguarded.
Volgens de leden van de PvdA-fractie is het element van privacy onvoldoende gewaarborgd.
Asks about storage and misuse of privacy-sensitive income data and the capacity of the Huurcommissie to handle more objections.
Can the government elaborate on the concerns about storing privacy-sensitive data?
Kan de regering nader ingaan op de zorgen rond de opslag van privacygevoelige gegevens?
Questions whether the informal flow of income information and the burden of proof on tenants comply with privacy rules and the ECHR.
Does this not create a risk of a large informal circuit supplying the landlord with information?
Ontstaat niet het risico van een groot informeel circuit om de verhuurder van informatie te voorzien?

Argues the use of tax data for rent purposes needs a formal legal basis and adequate safeguards under Article 8 ECHR and Article 10 of the Constitution, and questions how the Huurcommissie can verify income.
Article 8 ECHR requires that any interference with the right to respect for private life rest on a legal basis.
Artikel 8 van het EVRM eist dat iedere inmenging van het recht op respect voor privéleven op een wettelijke grondslag berust.
Doubts that misuse of data can be sufficiently limited, asks for justification of the pressing social need and alternatives, and asks for a hardship clause.
Under the ECHR the reason for a pressing social need must be justified.
Volgens het EVRM moet er gerechtvaardigd worden waarom er sprake is van «pressing social need».
Raises risks of privacy breaches, retroactive effect since 1 February 2012, absence of a rent-reduction or hardship procedure, and the one-sided burden on tenants.
Asks how landlords' access to income certificates is limited to their own dwellings and why objections go to the landlord rather than the Belastingdienst.
Why it is not possible for the tenant to object directly to the Belastingdienst.
Waarom het voor huurder niet mogelijk is direct bezwaar te maken bij de Belastingdienst.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division supports the bill allowing extra rent increases for high-income tenants of regulated dwellings but objects that it addresses only a partial problem of a dysfunctional housing market, lacks alternatives for the target group, and needs justification of the EUR 43,000 income threshold, household income definition, peiljaar and privacy safeguards. The government's nader rapport accepts several points (privacy, statement of the broader housing policy, income threshold rationale, peiljaar) but rejects the request to exclude other household members' income and the hardship clause, and treats the measure as part of a wider housing policy.
concerns: The Afdeling questions whether the one-sided measure, with only a negative incentive and no alternatives, can achieve its goal of improving mobility and is fair given that subsidies should primarily serve low incomes; the government adds explanation of wider policy and alternatives but keeps the measure.

The Afdeling doubts the measure will effectively promote housing mobility while the target group lacks realistic alternatives and corporations may not use the increase; the government explains expected effects and adds information on alternatives and corporate behaviour.
The Afdeling advises counting only the partner's income rather than all household members, which the government rejects as needed for a clear and reasonable household income concept.

The Afdeling asks for justification of the EUR 43,000 income threshold, which lies well above the EUR 33,614 social-housing target; the government explains the choice and amends the memorie van toelichting.
The Afdeling advises a hardship clause for tenants whose income falls below the threshold after the reference year, which the government declines because a clear, fixed reference year is needed.
The Afdeling asks for safeguards on personal data, including who has access and retention periods; the government adds access limits and a retention rule.
The Afdeling suggests moving the data-protection article to a separate chapter of the Uhw; the government adopts the editorial remark.

33138.s: The bill merges the municipalities of Graafstroom, Liesveld and Nieuw-Lekkerland into a new municipality called Molenwaard with effect from the date of reorganisation. It also adjusts related provisions on judicial districts, police and safety regions, electoral districts and transitional council elections.
q: With effect from the date of reorganisation, the municipalities of Graafstroom, Liesveld and Nieuw-Lekkerland are dissolved.
Met ingang van de datum van herindeling worden de gemeenten Graafstroom, Liesveld en Nieuw-Lekkerland opgeheven.
d: boundaries of new municipality shown on attached map

parties: Welcomes the merger and has no comments or questions.
They have no reason to make comments or ask questions.
Zij hebben geen aanleiding tot het maken van opmerkingen en tot het stellen van vragen.
Asks about regional consequences for Gorinchem, the financial position of Molenwaard, the Arhi payment schedule and whether the new municipality can itself decide on future mergers.
These members believe that municipal merger cannot be a goal in itself.
Deze leden zijn van mening dat herindeling niet een doel op zich kan zijn.
Questions the real level of popular support beyond council votes, regional effects, the financial risks of the merger and the transition problems faced by the municipalities.
They expect this structural reduction to be offset by the anticipated reduction in administrative costs and other efficiency gains of the new organisation.
Zij verwacht dat deze structurele verlaging opgevangen wordt door de te verwachten vermindering van de bestuurskosten en andere efficiencyvoordelen van de nieuwe organisatie.
Asks whether the legal framework is sufficient for a merger agreed at an early stage, how administrative burdens can be avoided, and what concrete steps address objections and financial risks.
Given that this is a merger that has already been arranged at an early stage, the SGP members wonder whether the legal framework for it is sufficient.
Gezien het feit dat er sprake is van een samenvoeging die al in een vroeg stadium tot stand gekomen is, vragen de leden van de SGP-fractie zich af of het wettelijk kader hiervoor voldoende is.

33165.s: The bill prohibits wearing face-covering clothing (such as burqas and niqabs) in public places, public transport, public-access buildings, schools and non-residential parts of care institutions, subject to listed exceptions for health, safety, occupation, sport, certain events and religious buildings. Violations are punishable by a first-category fine as a minor offence, with enforcement folded into routine police oversight and consultation on exemptions by the mayor.
33165.j: The memorandum justifies the ban by reference to open communication, equal treatment of men and women and social interaction, and the exemptions by health, safety, occupation and religious freedom.
q: The ban aims to remove obstacles to open communication and to promote equality between men and women.
Het verbod heeft tot doel belemmeringen voor open communicatie weg te nemen en gelijkwaardigheid van mannen en vrouwen te bevorderen.
d: mayor may exempt participants in events from the face-covering ban
p: Creates a general criminal prohibition restricting citizens' freedom of religion, expression and privacy, with exceptions that depend on administrative discretion of the mayor for events.
Sanctions the prohibition with a criminal fine enforced through routine police supervision and prosecution, with ordinary criminal procedure as a safeguard.

parties: Supports the ban as government's core duty to guarantee safety; asks whether 'other event' exemptions include commercial activities and how Belgian and French laws compare.
It is therefore necessary that the legislator takes this responsibility by curbing the objective and subjective safety risks caused by wearing face-covering clothing.
Het is daarom noodzakelijk dat de wetgever deze verantwoordelijkheid neemt door de objectieve en subjectieve veiligheid als gevolg van het dragen van gezichtsbedekkende kleding terug te dringen.

Questions whether the ban is needed, whether existing house rules and existing powers suffice, whether liberal freedom of expression is unjustly restricted, and who the real perpetrators of coercion are.
A general ban on expressing oneself in a way the majority of society dislikes is at odds with the freedom we all cherish for society as a whole.
Een algemeen verbod om je te uiten op een wijze die de meerderheid van de samenleving niet aanstaat, staat op gespannen voet met de vrijheid die we allemaal koesteren voor de samenleving als geheel.
Considers the fine too weak for burka-wearers and asks for a higher fine category and how identity and coercion will be established.
The PVV members, however, believe that this does not act forcefully enough against wearing a burka.
De leden van de PVV-fractie zijn echter van mening dat hiermee niet krachtig genoeg wordt opgetreden tegen het dragen van een boerka.

Accepts the legal basis and the open-communication aim but asks for careful balancing of religious freedom and proportionality, and whether voluntary-choice arguments and alternatives like information campaigns were considered.
Before the government can impose a ban limiting freedom of religion and freedom of expression, the CDA members consider it necessary to carefully weigh the different interests.

Alvorens de overheid een verbod in kan stellen dat de vrijheid van godsdienst en de vrijheid van meningsuiting beperkt, achten de leden van de CDA-fractie het noodzakelijk om nauwkeurig de verschillende belangen af te wegen.
Questions the evidence of criminality and the necessity and proportionality of a criminal ban as ultimum remedium, and whether the €390 fine and police discretion are justified.
The SP members share the Council of State's view that criminal law is an ultimum remedium.
De leden van de SP-fractie delen de mening van de Raad van State dat het strafrecht een ultimum remedium is.

Finds the four justifications weak, doubts the emancipation rationale and safety argument, notes the Council of State's negative advice was insufficiently answered, and warns of isolating effects on women.
Therefore these members are not convinced of the pressing social necessity of this ban, nor of why existing legislation would not be sufficient.
Derhalve zijn deze leden niet overtuigd van de klemmende maatschappelijke noodzaak van dit verbod, noch waarom bestaande wetgeving niet toereikend zou zijn.

Asks why a general ban was chosen over place-specific bans, questions compatibility with EVRM Article 9 proportionality and 'pressing social need', and whether existing powers were really insufficient.
These members ask the government to explain why it ignores the advice of the Council of State, namely not to send the bill to the House of Representatives.
Deze leden vragen de regering inzichtelijk te maken waarom zij het advies van de Raad van State, namelijk om het wetsvoorstel niet te zenden aan de Tweede Kamer, negeert.

Accepts that a ban may be warranted for public order and safety but questions the concrete problems addressed, the basis for the claimed rise in numbers, and the consistency of coercion-based reasoning with other clothing.
They do, however, have the necessary questions about this ban.
Zij hebben wel de nodige vragen bij dit verbod.

v.summary: The Council of State's advisory division advised against the bill introducing a general ban on face-covering clothing, finding the necessity of a general ban and its compatibility with freedom of religion (Art. 9 ECHR) insufficiently justified and advising reconsideration. The government's reply rejects the Council's objections, maintaining that the ban is necessary for open communication and equal participation, and that it is compatible with Article 9 ECHR.
concerns: The Council found no demonstrated pressing social need for a general criminal ban, and that existing specific bans and powers were not shown to be insufficient; the government disagreed, arguing general and uniform rules are needed.

The Council held the ban incompatible with freedom of religion under Article 9 ECHR because it was not shown to be necessary in a democratic society; the government maintained it is a justified and proportionate restriction.

The Council considered the criminal sanction unjustified as ultima remedium and questioned proportionality of a generic ban, while the government argued the restriction is limited to one specific expression and proportionate.

The Council objected that women's equality and emancipation cannot justify banning a choice freely made by the wearers, and that subjective feelings of insecurity cannot justify the ban; the government rejected the first point but accepted that subjective insecurity is not a standalone justification.

33192.s: The bill expands the power of Dutch immigration authorities to take and process facial images and fingerprints of foreign nationals for identity verification, adds new EU biometric regulations to the Vreemdelingenwet 2000, and creates rules on storage, provision to third parties and a five-year evaluation. It sets out that the detailed rules on how biometrics are taken and processed, and the procedures for data transfer and destruction, will be laid down by general administrative order (AMvB).
33192.j: The memorandum justifies the expanded biometric powers as improving reliable identity establishment of foreign nationals, referring to fraud, aliases and EU obligations, and states that privacy safeguards such as purpose limitation and retention periods are included.
d: manner of taking and processing facial images and fingerprints; measures if fingerprints cannot be obtained
rules on recording, forwarding and destruction of biometric data in the immigration administration
other numbers that administrative bodies may use when exchanging data, designated by regulation of the ministers
p: Authorises immigration officials to take a facial image and ten fingerprints from foreign nationals where necessary for identity establishment and verification, reducing bodily-integrity protection for non-EU nationals.

Lists limited purposes for which biometric data from the immigration administration may be made available to third parties, including criminal investigation, with prosecutorial conditions for fingerprint access.
Requires the minister to report to Parliament within five years on the effectiveness of the law and whether it should continue, which strengthens parliamentary oversight.

parties: Supports the aim of reliable identity checks but asks the government to clarify privacy safeguards, information security and protection of the central database.
However, these members consider some clarification from the government appropriate regarding safeguarding privacy.
Wel achten deze leden enige verduidelijking van de regering op zijn plaats in verband met het waarborgen van de privacy.
Welcomes the bill and asks questions, including on the ten-year retention period, which they would prefer to extend to twenty years for effective identity checks.
These members, however, consider it very important that biometric data of aliens be retained as long as possible for the most effective identity determination possible.
Voornoemde leden achten het echter van groot belang dat de biometrische gegevens van vreemdelingen zo lang mogelijk bewaard blijven met het oog op een zo effectief mogelijke identiteitsvaststelling.
Finds the balance between fraud prevention and fundamental rights (bodily integrity, privacy) justified given the safeguards and the privacy impact assessment, and awaits the evaluation.

In the view of these members, the elaboration of the described measures strikes a proper balance between preventing identity and document fraud and illegality on the one hand, and respecting the fundamental rights of the aliens concerned on the other.

Naar de mening van deze leden is bij de uitwerking van de beschreven maatregelen sprake van een juist evenwicht tussen enerzijds het streven naar het zoveel mogelijk voorkomen van identiteit- en documentfraude en illegaliteit en anderzijds de eerbiediging van de aan artikel 11 van de Grondwet, artikel 8 EVRM en artikel 3 EU-Handvest ontleende grondrechten van de betrokken vreemdelingen

Worries that purposes are elastic, that the database could become an investigation register, that exceptions are set by general administrative order rather than statute, and that fraud is not measured, so effectiveness cannot be judged.
Collecting biometric characteristics constitutes such an intrusion into persons' life and body that these members consider it important that exceptions also be regulated by statute.

Het verzamelen van biometrische kenmerken maakt een dusdanige inbreuk op het leven en lichaam van personen dat deze leden het belangrijk vinden dat ook uitzonderingen bij wet geregeld dienen te worden.
Questions necessity and proportionality, the broad purpose limitation (function creep), safeguards for criminal-investigation use and the wrongly-suspected alien, and the fit with EU and ECHR rules.
These members ask how the proposed extension relates to the rules and agreements made at European level on the use of biometrics for identifying aliens?
Deze leden vragen hoe de voorgestelde uitbreiding zich verhoudt tot de regels en afspraken die in Europees verband zijn gemaakt over de toepassing van biometrie ter identificatie van vreemdelingen?

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised in 2010 that the bill extending biometric data collection (face and ten fingerprints) for nearly all non-citizens in the immigration chain needed revision, mainly on effectiveness, fundamental rights (Article 8 ECHR and Dutch/EU rights), delegation and EU law. The government's nader rapport in 2012 accepted most points, narrowing retention, scope of disclosure, delegation and carrier obligations, and explained the remaining issues.
concerns: The Afdeling found effectiveness of ten-fingerprint collection across all categories insufficiently shown; the government added evidence from Eurodac and explained the rationale.
The explanatory memorandum inadequately weighed privacy interests under Article 8 ECHR and Marper; the government added a privacy impact assessment and fuller proportionality analysis.
The open-ended delegation for regulating biometric collection by AMvB was too broad; the government narrowed it and reserved new biometric identifiers for formal law.
The twenty-year retention period was too indefinite; the government reduced it to ten years with specified start points.

Differential treatment of family members of EU citizens and long-term residents conflicted with EU free movement and equal-treatment rules; the government adjusted family-member rules but justified the long-term residents approach.
Obligation on carriers to take biometrics was disproportionate and an encroachment on a core state task; the government dropped it.

Provisions on who may process data and for which purposes were insufficiently precise and risked function creep; the government clarified competent authorities and limited purposes, including Wbp purpose limitation.
Redactional and terminological corrections on verification versus identification and cross-references were adopted.

33219.s: The bill replaces the GBA population registry with a modernised basisregistratie personen, centralising data and rules for residents and, for the first time, allowing registration of non-residents for whom the Dutch state performs tasks. It sets out administrative duties, data supply, registration rights and data-sharing, leaving much technical detail to general administrative orders (AMvB).
33219.j: The memorandum justifies the broad use of AMvB delegation by the need to respond quickly to technical developments without repeatedly amending the statute.
q: By regulating this matter by or pursuant to a general administrative order, room has been created for further development of the basic person registration without having to amend the law each time.

Door deze materie bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur te regelen, is ruimte ontstaan voor verdere ontwikkeling van de basisregistratie personen, zonder hiervoor telkens de wet te hoeven aanpassen.
d: technical and administrative design, operation and security of the registry
categories of persons excluded from registration due to residence status
detailed list of general and administrative data items
designation of institutions allowing a postal address instead of residential address
categories and basis of cost contributions by bodies receiving data
p: The minister may investigate whether bodies receiving systematic data comply with registry rules, with carve-out for municipal bodies.
The mayor decides on safety grounds whether a person may use a postal address instead of a residential address.
Administrative decisions on correcting or disputing registered data are taken by the registering authority, subject to general appeal rules.

parties: Asks whether non-residents registered in the register are notified and can appeal, and how reliable the non-resident data is.
Will the persons concerned be notified, the VVD members ask, and will they then have the possibility to file objection and appeal against it?
Krijgen de personen die dat betreft, daar bericht van, zo vragen de leden van de VVD-fractie. Hebben deze personen vervolgens de mogelijkheid om daar bezwaar en beroep tegen aan te tekenen.

Argues that data sharing with third parties is defined too broadly ('gewichtig' or 'bijzonder maatschappelijk belang') and should be set in the act itself rather than lower regulation, to protect citizens' legal certainty and privacy.

The PvdA members also believe that the conditions, criteria and necessity for disclosing data to third parties must be defined more clearly and extensively and recorded as far as possible in the Wet BRP itself rather than in subordinate regulation.

De leden van de PvdA-fractie zijn tevens van mening dat de voorwaarden, criteria en noodzaak van de verstrekking van gegevens aan derden duidelijker en uitgebreider gedefinieerd moeten worden en zo veel mogelijk vastgelegd worden in de Wet BRP zelf en niet in onderliggende regelgeving.

Supports the reform but asks how the government will prevent shadow administrations, verify the adequacy of municipal safeguards against address fraud, and ensure thorough investigation of notifications.
How is it prevented that government bodies keep their own shadow administrations?
Hoe wordt voorkomen, dat overheidsorganen eigen schaduwadministraties bijhouden?

Worries that heavy reliance on general administrative measures and ministerial regulations makes the law less transparent and asks for an overview of all such delegated rules and for basic security rules to be placed in the act.
They request the government to list all general administrative measures and ministerial regulations, stating their purpose, the frameworks to be used and roughly what they will contain.

Zij verzoeken de regering om alle algemene maatregelen van bestuur en ministeriele regelingen op een rij te zetten en daarbij te vermelden wat het doel is, welke kaders gehanteerd zullen worden en hoe de invulling er grofweg uit zal zien.

Objects to vague definitions, delegation of core matters to later general administrative measures, insufficient privacy and security safeguards, and that the College bescherming persoonsgegevens was not consulted on a new power.
As far as these members are concerned, it is unthinkable that the government has sent the Chamber a bill in which the core of the bill can be unilaterally amended by the minister at a later date.

Wat deze leden betreft is het onvoorstelbaar dat de regering de Kamer nu een wetsvoorstel heeft gestuurd waarin de kern van het wetsvoorstel eigenhandig door de minister op een later tijdstip kan worden aangepast.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division supports the Basisregistratie personen bill but advises narrowing the delegation for providing data to third parties and revising or better justifying the administrative fine for information duties. The government reply adds a clarifying clause on third-party work of 'gewichtig maatschappelijk belang', better motivates the dual sanction regime, rejects the requested definitions of municipal and central facilities, and makes redactional corrections.
concerns: The broad delegation to regulate third-party data provision by AMvB is too vague; the criterion 'werkzaamheden met een gewichtig maatschappelijk belang' must be clarified in the law itself.
Data provision to third parties and the burgerservicenummer disclosure interfere with privacy under Article 8 ECHR and require a sufficiently specific legal basis.
Sanctioning similar information-duty violations through both administrative fines and criminal law is undesirable; the government justifies the dual regime rather than harmonising it.
Definitions of 'gemeentelijke voorziening' and 'centrale voorzieningen' should be included in the bill itself; the government declined, citing flexibility.
Redactional corrections to articles 3.16, 2.49 and cross-references, plus updated ministerial titles and footnotes.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised that the government's proposal to stop registering foreign nationality alongside Dutch nationality in the basic personal records (Wet basisregistratie personen) needed better justification, particularly for those who acquired Dutch nationality by operation of law and for keeping existing registrations. In its reply, the minister dropped the distinction by acquisition route and decided to stop recording foreign nationality for everyone, including existing records, in response to the Council's remarks.
concerns: The Council found the stated social problem of unwanted confrontation with foreign nationality insufficiently substantiated and asked for a fuller justification of the proposal or reconsideration.
The Council asked for a reasoned justification of the distinction between persons who acquired Dutch nationality by operation of law and those who acquired it by option or naturalisation.

The Council held that keeping existing registrations of foreign nationality for persons who acquired Dutch nationality by operation of law conflicts with the EU privacy directive's storage limitation principle.

The Council noted that the proposal merely shifts the problem, since authorities would still need to obtain foreign nationality data by other means, and that registration may be more important than the explanatory memorandum suggests.

33237.s: The bill adds a fifth paragraph to article 3:17 of the Wet op het financieel toezicht, allowing banks to use the burgerservicenummer (BSN) for keeping records that enable prompt payout under the deposit guarantee scheme and for supervision of those records. It implements EU Directive 2009/14/EC on deposit guarantee coverage and payout deadlines.
33237.j: The memorandum justifies the BSN use as necessary for prompt deposit payout and supervision, and assesses it against article 8 ECHR, articles 7 and 8 of the EU Charter and the Wbp, with the CBP raising no substantive objections.
q: The use of the BSN in the context of the DGS is therefore necessary in a democratic society.
Het gebruik van het BSN in het kader van het DGS is derhalve noodzakelijk in een democratische samenleving.
p: Allows banks to use the citizen service number for deposit guarantee administration when they hold it, with supervision by DNB, subject to a privacy assessment under article 8 ECHR and the Charter.

parties: Asks whether the privacy of clients remains adequately safeguarded when the BSN is linked to the DGS, and what safeguards the bill contains.
The VVD members ask the government whether the privacy of the customer remains sufficiently guaranteed when the citizen service number is linked to the DGS.
De leden van de VVD-fractie vragen de regering of de privacy van de klant voldoende gewaarborgd blijft wanneer het burgerservicenummer wordt gekoppeld aan het DGS.
Asks how the bill ensures banks use the BSN exclusively for the DGS and who supervises this.
Asks whether the BSN link could be extended to pre-filled tax returns and credit data, broadening use of the number for non-fiscal purposes.
The use of the citizen service number here concerns a non-fiscal purpose, the PVV members observe.
Het gebruik van het burgerservicenummer betreft hier een gebruik voor niet fiscale doeleinden, zo constateren de leden van de PVV-fractie.
Supports the shorter payout term and considers the BSN a suitable means within data protection rules, while asking whether less privacy-intrusive alternatives were considered.
For this purpose the use of the citizen service number appears a suitable means that fits both within the rules of the Personal Data Protection Act and the context of the ECHR.
Hiertoe lijkt het gebruik van het burgerservicenummer een geschikt middel dat zowel past binnen de regels van de Wet bescherming persoonsgegevens als binnen de context van het EVRM.
Asks about the maximum payout period, the certainty DNB can achieve, and what DNB oversight of bank administration involves in staffing terms.
How many full-time staff does DNB have available each year to supervise this?
Hoeveel fte heeft DNB jaarlijks ter beschikking om hierop toe te zien?
Weighs faster payout against depositors' privacy interests and asks whether depositors can object to BSN use and whether alternatives such as a client number were considered.
Faster payout is primarily in the customer's interest. However, the customer also has a privacy interest.
Het sneller uitbetalen is met name in het belang van de klant. De klant heeft echter ook nog een privacybelang.

33246.s: The bill amends the Dutch Act on international assistance in tax collection to implement EU Directive 2011/16/EU on administrative cooperation in taxation, covering information exchange on request, automatic and spontaneous exchange, simultaneous controls, serving documents, and the rules on confidentiality and use of information. It designates the Minister of Finance as competent authority and central liaison office, and adds general delegation powers for implementing rules by ministerial regulation.
33246.j: The memorandum justifies the delegation to ministerial regulation as a means to quickly implement Commission rules on implementation issues, stating that these can only concern implementation and cannot create new obligations.
q: This makes it possible to quickly implement, where necessary, the detailed rules of the European Commission.
Hierdoor wordt het mogelijk om, indien nodig, snel uitvoering te kunnen geven aan de nadere regels van de Europese Commissie.
d: further rules implementing chapter II on assistance requests
further rules implementing chapter III on forms of assistance
p: Allows information received under the Directive to be used for tax collection, social security contributions and penal procedures, and passed on to third states if the Minister judges it useful, subject to notice and a ten-day objection right for the source state.
Allows the Minister to forward information received from a state to other member states' authorities where useful, provided an agreement with the source state permits it.

Lets the Minister authorise a foreign authority to use exchanged information for purposes beyond tax collection, and to pass it to a third state, without a statutory standard for such authorisation beyond the stated grounds.

parties: Asks what other conditions apply to automatic data exchange and how far Dutch citizens' income data are protected and how its use is limited.
To what extent, for example, is income data of Dutch citizens protected?
In welke mate zijn bijvoorbeeld inkomensgegevens van de Nederlandse burgers beschermd?
Supports the aim of preventing double taxation and avoidance but asks how privacy is safeguarded in exchanges and whether companies should also be covered.
How exactly does this data exchange take place, and how is privacy guaranteed during the exchange?
Hoe vindt deze gegevensuitwisseling precies plaats, hoe wordt de privacy bij de uitwisseling gewaarborgd?
Asks whether the quid pro quo principle applies, what measures exist if a member state fails to comply, and what municipalities gain from inclusion.
What measures can be taken if a member state does not fulfil its obligations?
Welke maatregelen kunnen er worden genomen als een lidstaat zijn verplichtingen niet nakomt?
Welcomes automatic exchange but questions whether affected persons have adequate legal remedies, since the bezwaar option under the WIB seems limited.
Can the government confirm that the person to whom the information relates has no legal remedy?
Kan de regering bevestigen dat degene op wie de informatie betrekking is geen rechtsmiddel heeft?
Asks about the scope of the confidentiality duty, permitted uses of foreign-obtained information beyond tax purposes, and sanctions for improper use.
What is the sanction when the conditions are not followed?
Wat is de sanctie wanneer er niet volgens de voorwaarden wordt gehandeld?

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division supports the bill implementing Directive 2011/16/EU on administrative cooperation in tax matters, but raises points on differences from the directive (the definition of taxes and leges/retributies, the terugmelding obligation for automatically exchanged information) and on implementation dates. The Secretary of State's nader rapport accepts most of the advice, adapts the bill accordingly, and rejects the redactional point on deleting article 7(1)(d) with an explanation.
concerns: Article 29 (new) WIB on terugmelding for automatically obtained information should be brought into line with article 14(2) of the directive, and the government followed this.
The entry-into-force date for automatic exchange of information differs from the directive's 1 January 2015 date, and the article II wording was aligned with the directive.
Article II should clarify that the automatic exchange applies to tax periods starting from 1 January 2014, not merely to facts occurring from that date, and the government adjusted the provision.

The definition of taxes in article 1 WIB should explicitly exclude leges and retributies, as article 2(3) of the directive does; the government clarified this in the explanatory memorandum and redrafted article 5(1) rather than implementing the exclusion in article 1.
Redactional suggestions were made; the suggestion to delete article 7(1)(d) was not followed, while the suggestion on article 12(1) was adopted in part through redactional improvements.

33273.s: The bill implements Solvency II (Directive 2009/138/EC) into the Wft, revising insurer licensing, group supervision, capital requirements (SCR/MCR), reporting, recovery plans and supervisory powers, and creates a lighter 'Solvency II Basic' regime with exemptions for the smallest insurers. It also transfers detailed rule-making on many matters to general administrative orders (AMvB) and ministerial regulations.
33273.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations by the need for uniform EU implementation, proportionality, and the technical nature of the rules, and says the vast detail of the framework is set at the level of general administrative orders and ministerial regulations.
q: The directive follows the so-called Lamfalussy structure and therefore only covers the main lines of the supervisory framework.
De richtlijn volgt de zogenoemde Lamfalussy-structuur en omvat dus enkel de hoofdlijnen van het toezichtkader.
d: rules on DNB's task implementing binding EU acts
cooperation with foreign supervisory authorities and information sharing
full or partial exemption from licensing requirement
exemption from requirement for third-country insurers' branches
rules on public solvency and financial condition report
rules on valuation and coverage of technical provisions
DNB may exempt insurers from technical provisions rules
circumstances, calculation and effects of capital surcharge
DNB may impose capital surcharge in exceptional circumstances
DNB may extend recovery deadlines in market downturns
rules for group supervision of small insurers (fit and proper, reporting, sanctions)
p: Supervisor must notify other EU supervisors when a licence is revoked, aligning cross-border supervisory information flows.
DNB may verify information on-site at group companies and may only directly demand information from group members after first asking the Dutch insurer.
DNB may apply sanctions against insurance holdings and group members for solvency risks even where prudential rules are formally met, including at the request of a foreign group supervisor.
Adds grounds for licence withdrawal where an insurer fails minimum capital or short-term plan requirements, with DNB judging whether the plan is 'clearly inadequate'.
Supervisor may order insurers to increase technical provisions where they fail prescribed rules, and DNB may grant exemptions from technical provision rules.
DNB may impose capital surcharges on insurers in exceptional circumstances, with circumstances, calculation and effects deferred to a general administrative order.

DNB may restrict an insurer's free disposal of assets in several listed circumstances, including where an asset-liability shortfall is foreseen, with the insurer able to challenge only if the counterparty knew of the measure.
Ministerial regulation may grant full or partial exemptions from licensing requirements for certain insurers, with conditions attachable.

parties: Asks why the conduct-of-business supervision was left unchanged and about the intervention ladder and the group supervisor's powers relative to the recently adopted Interventiewet.
These members ask the government for further explanation of a number of parts of the bill.
Deze leden vragen de regering nadere toelichting op een aantal onderdelen van het wetsvoorstel.

Questions whether consumer protection is adequately safeguarded for small insurers exempted from supervision and asks about pro-cyclical effects of market valuation and the use of optional supervisory instruments.
Consumer protection must be the guiding principle, not merely the administrative burden on an insurer.
De bescherming van consumenten moet leidend zijn, niet louter de admini stratieve lasten voor een verzekeraar.
Asks technical questions about the abandonment of single-track reporting and the choice not to use certain member-state options.
Through this directive the so-called single-track principle for insurers is abandoned, the PVV members read.
Door deze richtlijn wordt de zogenaamde eensporigheid voor de verzekeraars losgelaten, zo lezen de leden van de PVV-fractie.
Welcomes the new framework but asks for a full overview of what is regulated by regulation versus minimum harmonisation, the use of national options, stress scenarios and costs.
The CDA members ask the government to give a complete overview of which matters will be regulated via regulation and which via minimum harmonisation.

De leden van de CDA-fractie vragen de regering een volledig overzicht geven welke zaken nu precies via een verordening worden geregeld zullen worden en welke zaken volgens minimumharmonisatie zullen verlopen.
Welcomes better protection of policyholders but asks how consumers are informed when small insurers are exempt from DNB supervision and about the scope of DNB's powers to prescribe measures.
Are requirements set on how the consumer is informed about this and on the moment at which the consumer is informed?
Worden er eisen gesteld aan de wijze waarop de consument hierover wordt voorgelicht en over het moment waarop de consument hierover wordt voorgelicht?

Asks about the consequences for policyholders of exemptions from supervision, about the scope for national choices given directly applicable EU regulations, and about the balance between micro- and macroprudential supervision.
The ChristenUnie members ask what the consequences are for the insured person/consumer.
De leden van de ChristenUnie-fractie vragen wat de consequenties zijn voor de verzekerde/consument.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory opinion on the Solvency II implementation bill raises concerns about enforcement against insurance holdings, the vague proportionality principle, cross-border activity of small insurers, supervision of third-country groups, natura-uitvaart insurers, and the Zvw. The minister's reply largely accepts the remarks, redrafts article 1:58e, drops the statutory proportionality clause, and expands the explanatory memorandum.
concerns: Article 1:58e enforcement against the holding relied on unspecified foreign provisions, raising nulla poena concerns; the reply removes that wording and refers directly to the directive.
The proportionality principle was insufficiently defined in the bill; the government dropped the statutory clause and added examples to the explanatory memorandum.
Cross-border activity of small insurers implied access to the European passport; the articles were redrafted to make clear they fall outside the directive's scope.
Unspecified 'other methods' for supervising third-country groups needed explanation; the explanatory memorandum was supplemented.
Supervision of group structures containing natura-uitvaart insurers was unclear and the memorandum was supplemented.
Whether article 206 of the directive still permits Zvw public-interest justification needed clarification; the memorandum now states the provisions are virtually identical.
Numerous redactional and cross-reference remarks in the annex were accepted and incorporated.

33282.s: The bill amends the Telecommunicatiewet and the Wet OPTA so that the regulator OPTA keeps its supervisory role over the EU roaming regulation, by replacing the reference to the old regulation 717/2007 with an abstract reference to any roaming regulation and its implementing acts. It also requires the minister to publish the title, source and entry-into-force date of the roaming regulation in the Staatscourant.
33282.j: The memorandum justifies the abstract reference by noting that the EU regulation is directly binding and that a future replacing regulation must remain covered without a new amendment to national law.
q: For this reason an abstract reference was chosen that takes into account the possibility that a future policy change on roaming is laid down in a new regulation replacing the third roaming regulation.

Gelet op bovenstaande is in dit wetsvoorstel gekozen voor een abstracte verwijzing die rekening houdt met de mogelijkheid dat een toekomstige beleidswijziging op het gebied van roaming wordt neergelegd in een nieuwe verordening die de derde roamingverordening vervangt.
d: publication of title, source and entry-into-force date of the roaming regulation

v.summary: The Raad van State advised on a bill amending the Telecommunications Act to implement the third EU roaming regulation, supporting its aim but objecting that binding BEREC guidelines went beyond EU law and recommending deletion of that reference. The government reply reports that the Council's advice was followed in the bill and explanatory memorandum, with additional drafting corrections.
concerns: Giving BEREC guidelines the same binding force as the regulation goes beyond what EU law requires and should be dropped from the bill.
Various drafting corrections to the bill and explanatory memorandum, including the considerans wording and notification references.

33291.s: The bill amends the Environmental Management Act to set CO2 emission allocations per greenhouse horticulture establishment (inrichtingsallocatie) instead of only collectively, with compensation payments and reimbursements. Detailed rules on allocation, fees, compensation and use of the proceeds are delegated to general administrative orders (AMvB).
33291.j: The memorandum explains that the allocation factors and compensation rules will be set in the AMvB because they are detailed, technical rules tied to the sectoral emission space.
d: categories and method for setting CO2 emission allocation per establishment
rules on compensation payments and reimbursements, including amounts
purposes and rules for using money obtained from compensation
p: Allows an AMvB to determine the purposes for which compensation money is spent, without statutory specification of those purposes.

parties: Asks about level playing field effects, sector support, and whether the productschap-based implementation accounts for possible abolition of productschappen.
The VVD members ask whether account has been taken of the possible abolition of the productschappen in this regard.</br>
De leden van de VVD-fractie vragen of hierbij rekening gehouden is met het eventueel afschaffen van de productschappen.
Supports the system for CO2 reduction and lower administrative burden, asking about incentives for lagging firms and use of any revenue.
The members are positive about introducing the proposed system because it leads to CO2 savings with individual firms given an incentive to invest in this.</br>
De leden zijn positief over de invoering van het voorgestelde systeem omdat het leidt tot CO 2 -besparing waarbij individuele bedrijven een prikkel krijgen om hierin te investeren.
Has no questions or comments on the bill.
The PVV members have taken note of the bill and currently have no need to ask questions or make comments.</br>
De leden van de PVV-fractie fractie hebben kennisgenomen van het wetsvoorstel en hebben thans geen behoefte aan het stellen van vragen en het maken van opmerkingen.
Calls the system creative but raises concerns about investment certainty for individual growers tied to sector-wide performance, and asks about compensation rules and state-aid risk.
Has no questions at this stage.
The SP members have taken note of the bill and currently have no need to ask questions.</br>
De leden van de SP-fractie hebben kennis genomen van het genoemde wetsvoorstel en hebben thans geen behoefte aan het stellen van vragen

Questions the rationale for opting out of the ETS, the risk of rewarding high historical emissions, arbitrage by growers, reliance on a productschap regulation instead of statute, and state-aid and energy-tax implications.
These members ask the government to also describe, for existing firms, how the system could most simply be decoupled from historical emissions.</br>
Deze leden vragen de regering om ook voor bestaande bedrijven te omschrijven op welke wijze de systematiek het meest eenvoudig losgekoppeld kan worden van historische emissies
Has no questions at this stage.
The GroenLinks members have taken note of the bill and currently have no need to ask questions.</br>
De leden van de GroenLinks-fractie hebben kennisgenomen van het genoemde wetsvoorstel en hebben thans geen behoefte aan het stellen van vragen.
Has no questions at this stage.
The ChristenUnie members have taken note of the bill and currently have no need to ask questions.</br>
De leden van de ChristenUnie-fractie hebben kennisgenomen van het genoemde wetsvoorstel en hebben thans geen behoefte aan het stellen van vragen.

33309.s: The bill amends the Dutch Criminal Code to implement EU Directive 2011/36/EU on human trafficking, extending Dutch jurisdiction over trafficking offences committed abroad by nationals and residents, broadening the definition of exploitation and vulnerable position, and adding violence as an aggravating circumstance. It also includes coordinating provisions with a separate pending bill on forced marriage, polygamy and female genital mutilation, depending on which enters into force first.
33309.j: The memorandum justifies the changes as required implementation of the EU directive, with the prosecutor and judge retaining discretion in applying the vulnerability definition and sentencing.
q: The directive instrument adds value in that it provides the stronger binding force that the EU legal order creates.
Het instrument van de richtlijn heeft als meerwaarde dat wordt voorzien in de sterkere bindende kracht die de rechtsorde van de Europese Unie tot stand brengt

parties: Asks who monitors compliance with the directive and whether the national rapporteur's independence is guaranteed in other member states.
It must be prevented that the national rapporteur in other member states is an intrinsic part of a ministry's organisation or even a civil servant assigned this task.
Voorkomen moet worden dat de nationaal rapporteur in andere lidstaten een intrinsiek onderdeel is van de organisatie van een bepaald ministerie of zelfs een ambtenaar die met deze taak wordt belast.
Asks why the NRM's suggestion to criminalise clients of trafficking victims was not adopted and how enforcement would work.
These members ask whether, besides the stated argument that direct criminalisation of clients would be problematic for enforcement, there are other reasons not to follow up the NRM's suggestion.

Deze leden vragen of er, naast het geformuleerde argument dat een rechtstreekse strafbaarstelling van de klant vanuit het oogpunt van handhaving problematisch zou zijn, nog andere redenen zijn om geen verdere uitvoering te geven aan de overweging van de NRM.
Objects to EU Commission sanctions on member states and to EU competence over national criminal law, and wants Dutch control over the B9 residence regime.
These members believe the European Parliament and the Council should interfere as little as possible with national legislation.
Deze leden zijn van mening dat het Europees Parlement en de Raad zich minimaal met nationale regelgeving zouden moeten bemoeien.
Asks whether victim interviews should be mandatorily recorded audiovisually and raises the lack of enforceable rights for victims and shelter waiting lists.
These members share the Raad voor de rechtspraak's view that interviews of trafficking victims acting as witnesses should practically always be recorded audiovisually.
De leden van de SP-fractie delen de mening van de Rvdr dat verhoren van slachtoffers van mensenhandel die als getuige optreden eigenlijk altijd audiovisueel geregistreerd zouden moeten worden.
Welcomes the aggravating circumstance for crimes against particularly vulnerable victims and has no further questions for now.
Taking all this into account, the CDA members currently have no questions or comments.
Dit alles overziende hebben de leden van de CDA-fractie vooralsnog geen vragen of opmerkingen.
Asks about securing the national rapporteur's independence by statute, data for the NRM, and the Council of State's concern about the non-punishment principle.
The D66 members ask the government to explain why it chose to incorporate the non-punishment principle from article 8 of the directive into the proposed amendment of the trafficking guideline.

De leden van de D66-fractie verzoeken de regering nader uiteen te zetten waarom ervoor wordt gekozen om het non punishment-beginsel zoals dat is verwoord in artikel 8 van de richtlijn te betrekken bij de voorgenomen wijziging van de Aanwijzing Mensenhandel.
Supports tougher criminal law and suggests further tightening, including criminalising clients and aligning the age threshold with the prostitution bill.
These members support tightening Dutch criminal law on trafficking and share the government's view that this is modern slavery.
Deze leden steunen de aanscherping van de Nederlandse strafwetgeving ter zake van mensenhandel en delen de visie van de regering dat hier sprake is van moderne slavernij.
Asks whether the anti-trafficking approach is fragmented across international bodies and about the continuity of exit programmes and prosecution sentencing.
The SGP members ask whether the approach to trafficking is not very fragmented.
De leden van de SGP-fractie vragen of de aanpak van mensenhandel niet erg versnipperd is.

v.summary: The Raad van State's Afdeling advisering supports the bill implementing Directive 2011/36/EU on human trafficking but objects to raising the basic offence's maximum penalty beyond what the directive requires and to limiting the aggravating circumstance to children under sixteen, and asks for clearer implementation of victim-protection obligations. The government's nader rapport accepts most of this advice: it adjusts the aggravating circumstance to follow the directive more closely, supplements the explanatory memorandum on victim assistance, and adds a provision on overlap with a parallel bill.
concerns: The Afdeling objected that raising the basic offence's maximum penalty to ten years is not required by the directive and must be justified, given conflicting proposals for twelve years.
The Afdeling advised extending the aggravating circumstance beyond children under sixteen to cover victims up to eighteen, in line with the directive's intent on particularly vulnerable victims.
The Afdeling asked that the explanatory memorandum show the binding normative framework for victim shelter and assistance obligations, which are implemented largely through practice.
The Afdeling asked that statements in the transposition table that a provision needs no implementation be explained more fully.

33318.s: The bill simplifies several Dutch social security laws (child benefit, survivors' benefits, old-age pension, and related schemes) by abolishing the separate half-orphan benefit, merging it into a higher survivors' benefit, and tightening age and education conditions for child benefit for 16- and 17-year-olds. It also sets income thresholds, allows ministerial rules on school enrolment and split payments, and adjusts cross-references in many related acts.
33318.j: The memorandum justifies the delegated rules as needed to reduce implementation costs and administrative burden, and to clarify how the new income and school conditions apply in practice.
q: Rules may be laid down by ministerial regulation on the interpretation of the second paragraph.
Bij ministeriële regeling kunnen nadere regels worden gesteld met betrekking tot de invulling van het tweede lid.
d: details of education conditions for 16-17 year olds
income threshold and rules on child income for 16-17 year olds
contribution amount and rules for doubled child benefit
cases in which child benefit may be split between parents
rules converting partial calendar years into full years of insurance
p: The conditions for child benefit for 16-17 year olds lapse on a date to be set by royal decree, leaving the timing of the change to the executive.
The survivors' benefit is recalculated to a net 90% of minimum wage for certain survivors, which reduces the benefit for many beneficiaries without parliamentary debate on each case.
Artikel II.G (Art. 27 et seq. Anw, paragrafen 3 en 4 vervallen)
Entire paragraphs on the half-orphan benefit are removed, eliminating a distinct statutory entitlement that citizens could previously rely on.

parties: Supports simplifying rules and few exceptions but asks about EU rights, buy-out options and child benefit spending effects.
They also consider it important that, as the government proposes, rules are based on main rules with as few exceptions as possible.
Daarnaast vinden zij het van belang dat – zoals de regering voorstelt – regels zijn gemaakt op hoofdregels, met zo weinig mogelijk uitzonderingen.
Worries the consequences for benefit recipients may be considerable and asks about income losses for surviving parents and the reasons for exceptions.
They believe the consequences for benefit recipients may be considerable, and that this is then not a simplification of regulations.
Zij menen dat de gevolgen voor uitkeringsgerechtigden aanzienlijk kunnen zijn, en dat dan niet om een vereenvoudiging van regelingen gaat.
Asks about effects on SVB supervision, the number of exception cases, bilateral treaties and how details will be set in lower regulation.
Do the proposals to simplify and abolish regulations have consequences for the way supervision is carried out?
Hebben de voorstellen om regelgeving te vereenvoudigen en af te schaffen gevolgen voor de wijze van toezicht?

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division supports the Wet vereenvoudiging regelingen SVB but raises objections on co-parent split payments, compensation for abolishing double child benefit, integration of the half-orphan benefit, the AOW minimum-residence rule, property-rights review, and transitional law. The minister's reply largely accepts the points: double child benefit abolition was dropped, the AOW motivation and transitional wording were revised, and co-parent split payments were retained with added justification.
concerns: The Afdeling asked for reasoned justification for keeping split child-benefit payments for co-parents, which the government supplied and kept the arrangement with added reasoning.
Abolishing double child benefit without a compensation plan could cause sudden income loss; the government dropped the abolition.
The Afdeling asked for integrated review under the EU Charter and Protocol 1 ECHR; the government added some property-right reasoning but judged full Charter review not warranted.

The transitional period for double child benefit should run from entry into force rather than publication, and the wording should state the six-month term clearly; the government revised the transitional provision.
The AOW one-year minimum needed justification other than lack of sufficient residence ties; the government revised the rationale to administrative cost.
Regulation 883/2004 exceptions for the AOW minimum period needed explanation; the government added a passage noting unknown affected numbers.
Several technical and redactional corrections were proposed and largely incorporated.

33327.s: The bill simplifies several social security laws (Werkloosheidswet, Ziektewet, WWIK, and related acts) by redefining working hours and wage-based criteria, shifting qualifying tests to hours worked and adjusting benefit calculations, and it introduces a calamity regime for unworkable weather with ministerial regulation setting details. It also reduces the benefit of unemployed people who start self-employed work by a fixed 29% and lets ministerial and general administrative regulations set key criteria and percentages.
33327.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations as allowing quick adjustment in practice and matching ministerial regulations to changing circumstances, such as calamities, while keeping budgetary neutrality.
q: This calamity regulation will be set out in a ministerial regulation based on the articles mentioned above, so that it can be quickly adjusted if circumstances give cause to do so.

Deze calamiteitenregeling zal worden vormgegeven in een ministeriële regeling gebaseerd op de hiervoor genoemde artikelen, zodat zij snel kan worden aangepast als omstandigheden daartoe aanleiding geven.
d: Artikel I, A (art. 1 WW) and B (art. 1a)
which hours count as working hours and equated hours
equating non-worked hours with working hours
Artikel I, O and P (art. 35ab WW)
lower percentage reduction of benefit for starters
calamity unemployment benefit rules and exemption from short-time work ban
Artikel III, D and C (WWIK art. 15, 58)
rules fixing number of working hours and days with wages
exemption from short-time work prohibition under extraordinary circumstances, with conditions
Artikel I, I (art. 20 WW) and Artikel VIII (Ziektewet art. 29f)
further rules on dagloon and working hour calculations
p: Artikel I, G (art. 18 WW) and Artikel V, A (BBA art. 8)

The minister may exempt employers from the short-time work ban in extraordinary circumstances and set benefit rules by ministerial regulation, with rules able to set aside the normal eligibility conditions.
A general administrative order may lower the fixed 29% benefit reduction for starters, changing benefit levels without statutory change.
Artikel I, A and B (art. 1, 1a WW) and Artikel III, B
The ministerial regulation determines which hours are equated with working hours, affecting eligibility.
Artikel I, W (art. 135b WW) and Artikel I, V (transitional)
A transitional provision keeps prior starter rules for a limited period of five years.

parties: Asks technical questions on how entitlement to income from work counts as an hour, the choice of conversion factor, daily wage reference periods, and the start-up scheme's duration.
The VVD members do still have some questions about the bill.
De leden van de VVD-fractie hebben wel nog enkele vragen over het wetsvoorstel.

Objects that removing the monthly deduction for court dismissal cases discourages workers from challenging dismissals in court, and that tightened criteria are a cut in benefits rather than simplification.

The PvdA members believe the government deliberately wants to make it harder for dismissed workers to go to the cantonal court and discourage them from challenging dismissals, whether justified or not.;

De leden van de PvdA-fractie zijn van mening dat de regering bewust ontslagen werknemers hun gang tot de kantonrechter wil bemoeilijken en wil ontmoedigen al dan niet onterecht ontslag aan te vechten.
Supports simplification but questions the tightening to 208 hours, which may disadvantage flexible workers, and asks whether the sanction for fraud under the calamity scheme remains robust.
The tightening of this requirement to 208 hours appears to conflict with the bill's starting point, namely that effects on benefits should be kept as small as possible.

De verzwaring van deze eis tot 208 uren lijkt op gespannen voet te staan met het uitgangspunt van de wet, namelijk dat ernaar gestreefd wordt om de effecten op de uitkeringen zo klein mogelijk te houden.

v.summary: The Council of State's advisory division supports the bill simplifying UWV benefit rules but objects to the calamity scheme, in particular a five-year exclusion of employers for fraud, which it considers a punitive sanction under Article 6 ECHR, disproportionate, and lacking a formal statutory basis, and it also questions the extended payment period. The government's reply accepts these points by dropping the exclusion, adding a clarification and an advance-payment option, and making technical changes.
concerns: The five-year exclusion of employers from the calamity scheme after fraud is disproportionate and may be counterproductive, so it should be reconsidered; the government dropped the exclusion.
The exclusion is a punitive sanction (criminal charge under Article 6 ECHR) that must be laid down in a formal statute, not in a ministerial regulation; the government abandoned the plan.
A statutory basis for the exclusion in the BBA 1945 is lacking, since the terms 'beperkingen' and 'voorschriften' do not cover exclusion from the scheme.

Extending the payment period from six to fourteen weeks may leave workers without income for longer, and the explanatory memorandum should mention advance payments; the government added the advance-payment option.
Several redactional and cross-reference corrections were recommended and have been incorporated.

33336.s: The bill amends several education statutes (primary, secondary, vocational, higher education and media law) mainly to fix technical errors, remove or replace open-ended delegations that allow departures from statute by lower regulation (following the Jurgens motion), delete spent transitional provisions, and update ministry names. It also contains coordination clauses for other pending bills.
33336.j: The memorandum justifies the changes by the Jurgens motion of the Eerste Kamer, which asked the government to stop using delegations that allow departures from statute, and it explains that many changes are technical or consolidating.
q: The motion asks the government to no longer use legislation that authorises lower legislators to make rules deviating from the statute.
In deze motie wordt de regering verzocht geen vorm van wetgeving meer te gebruiken waarbij de wetgever lagere wetgevers machtigt om regels te stellen die afwijken van de wet.
d: making articles of the WVO applicable to certain school types
rules on appointment or employment of teachers without appointment for non-core subjects
funding rules for school communities and cursus-linked schools
rules for school communities under the vocational education act
minister may permit examination questions not to be made available
making articles of the WVO BES applicable to certain school types
p: Removes open-ended power to deviate from statute by lower regulation, restoring legislative control over the rules.
Relocates still-applicable transitional rules into the statute, improving legal certainty.

parties: The VVD asks the government to respond to the municipality's arguments that the school would be closed if its exemption lapses, and that it does not meet the legal cooperative school structure.
The members would welcome a response from the government to these arguments.
De leden ontvangen graag een reactie van de regering op deze argumenten.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised, while endorsing the bill's aim, to revise how the Jurgens motion is implemented (restricting scope before allowing ministerial override), to add a separate transitional-law chapter to the WPO and WEC, and to clarify temporary provisions such as the Earnewâld cooperative school article. The government reply accepted most points, rejected none outright, and explained the changes made, including removing the Earnewâld exception and tightening the school-council consent wording.
concerns: Ministerial power to set aside statutory provisions by lower regulation conflicts with the Jurgens motion; the Afdeling asked for scope restriction in the law itself and no re-declaration of already applicable provisions.

Transitional law is scattered through substantive provisions and includes spent or incomplete rules, reducing knowability; the Afdeling advised a separate transitional chapter and review of completeness.

Temporary provision on the Earnewâld cooperative school was made permanent without explaining its temporary nature or its links to laws now in force; the Afdeling asked for clarification or adjustment.
Numerous redactional remarks on wording, cross-references and transitional provisions, most adopted, with some remarks not taken over and explained in the reply.

33345.s: The bill proposes amending the Dutch Constitution to reduce the Tweede Kamer from 150 to 100 seats and the Eerste Kamer from 75 to 50 seats, with transitional provisions tying the change to the first sitting of newly elected chambers. It contains no delegation of rule-making power to the executive.
33345.j: The memorandum justifies the reduction by arguing that smaller chambers can still fulfil their legislative and control roles and that focusing on main lines improves oversight, while noting the cost of transitional allowances.
q: The proposed reduction does not mean that the States General can no longer fulfil its role as representative body in a good way.
De voorgestelde verkleining leidt er niet toe dat de Staten-Generaal zijn rol van volksvertegenwoordiging niet meer op een goede manier kan vervullen.

v.summary: The Council of State advisory division advises against sending the bill reducing Parliament's seats (Tweede Kamer 150 to 100, Eerste Kamer 75 to 50) to the House without first addressing its objections on constitutional readiness, the lack of a sufficient justification, and transitional arrangements. The government reply rejects the claim that the explanatory memorandum lacks a sufficient justification, while adding arguments and supplementing the memorandum on effectiveness, savings and transitional law.
concerns: The bill lacks a sufficient justification reflecting Parliament's special constitutional position, and the constitutional readiness of the change is not demonstrated; the government argues the idea has sufficient constitutional maturity.

The stated aims (savings of EUR 6 million, reduced administrative burden) are doubtful in effectiveness, and side effects such as extra support costs are not addressed; the government supplements the memorandum but disputes the conclusion.
