De Raad van State geeft echter aan dat met de voorgestelde maatregel dit doel maar in beperkte mate kan worden bereikt.
Asks whether a capacity (doenvermogen) test was done for clients and whether alternatives to removing the double-intent requirement were considered.
These members ask whether alternatives were considered by the government to achieve the intended aim and if so, which alternatives these are.
Deze leden vragen of er alternatieven zijn overwogen door de regering om het beoogde doel te bereiken en zo ja, welke alternatieven dat zijn.
Warns that clawback against clients could wrongly burden people accused of fraud and deter use of care, and asks for safeguards against overzealous enforcement.
What safeguards are there to prevent people from becoming victims of an overzealous fraud hunt?
Welke waarborgen zijn er om te voorkomen dat mensen de dupe worden van een doorgeschoten fraudejacht?

v.summary: The Council of State's advisory division advised on a draft bill amending the Jeugdwet and Wmo 2015 to remove the double-intent requirement for recovering unlawfully obtained care funds and to create a legal basis for care providers and the CAK to share personal data of uninsured persons with GGDs and municipalities. The government's reply accepts the key objection, moving the detailed data rules and retention periods from ministerial regulation to an AMvB, while defending necessity and effectiveness and adding clarifications.
concerns: Processing of medical and personal data of uninsured persons and the breach of medical confidentiality must be regulated at least by AMvB given the right to privacy under Article 10 of the Constitution; the government moved the rules to an AMvB but defended the necessity of the data sharing.

The removal of the double-intent requirement will have limited effectiveness, since recovery is only possible after a benefit is withdrawn for incorrect data; the explanatory memorandum was expanded to clarify this.

Necessity and proportionality of the proposed data processing for GGDs and the CAK, including the opt-out system, were insufficiently reasoned; the government sharpened the explanatory memorandum but did not change the opt-out design.

Expanded recovery powers could reach providers who acted in good faith; the explanatory memorandum was clarified that recovery from providers is not automatic and that administrative law safeguards apply.
Essential data categories and retention periods should not be left to a ministerial regulation; the bill was amended to provide for an AMvB.

36702.s: The bill amends the Wabvpz and Jeugdwet to create registers of healthcare and youth-care providers and staff, and a framework for approving high-assurance login means for digital access to health information systems. It lets the Minister approve login means, sets up a mandatory use requirement for these means, and extends IGJ supervision to the approval regime.
36702.j: The explanatory memorandum justifies the broad delegation to AMvBs by the need for technical detail, flexibility for different login means, and realistic implementation timelines.
d: registration, refusal/suspension/withdrawal, data processing and fees for the healthcare register
proof of high assurance level, application and approval procedures for login means
detailed rules on the electronic notification channel
access to and use of systems with approved login means, designation of systems
youth-care provider register: registration, procedures, data processing, fees
access to and use of youth-care systems and login-means linkage
timing of the mandatory use of high-assurance login means
p: The Minister gains discretion to approve, refuse, suspend or withdraw login means, with the criteria left largely to an AMvB.
Care providers and staff must use only approved login means for the specified systems, a mandatory requirement set by the executive.
Art. I B (art. 14, lid 4 sub b)
Procedures and grounds for refusing, suspending or withdrawing register entries are delegated to an AMvB, with an appeal route via the general administrative law framework.

parties: Asks which concrete problems the bill solves, why legislation is needed rather than sector agreements, and who oversees implementation.
The PVV members ask which concrete problems this proposal solves and whether alternative solutions were considered.
De leden van de PVV-fractie vragen welke concrete problemen met dit voorstel worden opgelost, en zijn er alternatieve oplossingen overwogen.

Pushes for justification of the bill, transparency of approvals, adequate IGJ resourcing, privacy safeguards, patient rights to information on access to their data, and limits on lending of login means and use of private phones.
The GroenLinks-PvdA members ask the government to explain how it will stimulate, monitor and evaluate the transition to Dezi means.
De leden van de GroenLinks-PvdA-fractie vragen de regering om toe te lichten hoe zij de overstap naar Dezi-middelen gaat stimuleren, monitoren en evalueren.

Sees data exchange as essential but asks about security against cybercrime and diploma fraude, the role of paramedics, DigiD resilience against DDoS attacks, and how approved means are checked for safety.
This must however happen in a safe way, certainly given the increase in cybercrime and (diploma) fraud in healthcare.
Dit moet echter wel op een veilige manier gebeuren, zeker met het oog op de toename van cybercrime en (diploma)fraude in de zorg.
Asks why voluntary participation applies beyond the SBV-Z, whether purpose limitation and algorithm use are controlled, and how malware and data protection are ensured.
May the data in the Dezi-register also be used for other purposes?
Mag de data in het Dezi-register ook voor andere doeleinden worden gebruikt?
Has taken note of the bill and has no questions for the government.
These members have no questions for the government.
Deze leden hebben geen vragen aan de regering.
Asks whether the bill's choices reflect binding law or policy, why the 'substantieel' level is excluded, why unified login via DigiD is not preferred, and how dependence on non-EU actors is reduced.
These members ask whether the government shares this starting point, also in light of geopolitical developments.
Genoemde leden vragen of de regering dit uitgangspunt deelt, mede in het licht van de geopolitieke ontwikkelingen.
Asks which personal data healthcare workers can access, what safeguards prevent excessive profits and vendor lock-in with private ICT providers, and whether a fully public system was examined.
What safeguards have been built in to prevent excessive profits and vendor lock-ins?
Welke waarborgen zijn er ingebouwd om buitensporige winsten hiermee en vendor lock-ins te voorkomen?
Supports standardisation and the Afdeling advisering's recommended mandatory use, and the option of phased start dates, and has no further questions for now.
The SGP members support this tightening.
De leden van de SGP-fractie steunen deze aanscherping.

Asks who bears responsibility if high-level identification risks materialise, how audits of BSN misuse are conducted, hosting contract continuity and EU data protection, and EUDI wallet interoperability.
Can the government specifically indicate which risks remain after implementation of this level?
Kan de regering echter specifiek aangeven welke risico's resteren na implementatie van dit niveau?
Has no further questions or remarks on the first and second nota van wijziging.
They have no further questions or remarks for the government.
Zij hebben geen verdere vragen of opmerkingen aan de regering.

Asks about cybersecurity risks from private phones, realism of certification timelines, costs and structural compensation, usability of UZI passes, patient access rights to their data, administrative burden, and BES implementation.
They therefore ask what fallback options or temporary means care providers can expect in case of acute temporary staffing, for which a one to two day application time is too long.
Zij vragen daarom welke terugvalopties of tijdelijke middelen zorgaanbieders kunnen verwachten in het geval van acute inhuur, waarvoor één tot twee dagen aanvraagtijd te lang duurt.

Asks whether national security and strategic autonomy safeguards are sufficient given geopolitics, whether at least some login means should be fully European, whether vendors should be limited to approved suppliers, and why the phased entry into force was postponed to 2031.
These members ask whether the government considers it wise that at least one or a few login means are fully in European hands and whose use the government can stimulate.
Deze leden vragen of de regering het verstandig acht dat er tenminste één of enkele inlogmiddelen zijn die volledig in Europese handen zijn, en waarvan de regering het gebruik kan stimuleren.

Argues the bill imposes very burdensome obligations, costs and technical requirements on a strained sector, questions feasibility for small providers and rural regions, shifting transition dates, dependence on commercial vendors, and asks for exemptions.

Asks whether regulation should be tightened so only software from companies established in the Netherlands or Europe may be used, the legal options for this, and the extent of dependence on non-European vendors for critical healthcare functions.

They ask the government whether it would not be preferable, from a strategic autonomy perspective, to tighten regulation on this point so that only software from companies actually established in the Netherlands or Europe may be used.

De leden van de SGP-fractie vragen de regering of het niet wenselijker is om vanuit het perspectief van strategische autonomie regelgeving op dit punt aan te scherpen zodat alleen gebruik kan worden gemaakt van software van bedrijven die daadwerkelijk in Nederland of in Europa gevestigd zijn.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised that the bill creating the Dezi-register should require identification and authentication with an approved high-assurance login means also for access to care information systems and electronic exchange systems, not only the SBV-Z, and set a deadline for this. The minister's reply accepts this advice, adds a power to set per-system implementation dates by AMvB, and extends the transitional arrangement for UZI-means to 1 January 2028.
concerns: The Afdeling expects the bill to contribute only limitedly to secure, high-assurance access to client data because registration is required only for the SBV-Z and not for care information systems.

The Afdeling considers that the protection of special personal health data warrants a binding deadline rather than relying on the voluntary character of the scheme, given the burden on care providers.
The Afdeling notes that transitional arrangements are needed so that UZI-means and the new Dezi-register can coexist without a gap in available login means.

36711.s: The bill requires banks with more than three million Dutch payment account holders to maintain a nationwide cash infrastructure with fair, non-discriminatory access, and lets the government set tariffs and conditions by general administrative order. It also lets DNB monitor cash-transport continuity, designate large cash-transport firms, and enforce obligations on them through reporting, approval-type delays, wind-down plans and fines.
36711.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations by the need for flexibility to respond to unforeseen market and technological developments in cash services and continuity risks.
q: For this reason the bill allows rules to be set at decree level on how customers may use the cash infrastructure.
Daarom biedt het wetsvoorstel de mogelijkheid om op besluitniveau regels te stellen over de manier waarop klanten gebruik kunnen maken van de chartale basisinfrastructuur.
d: details and requirements of the cash infrastructure facilities
tariffs banks may charge for use of cash infrastructure, may be set at zero
conditions banks may impose on customers using cash infrastructure
content, form, frequency and deadlines of information to DNB
exemption from cash infrastructure obligations, with attached rules
breakdown of location reporting by region or sector
regional or sectoral designation threshold for cash-transport firms
timing and content of semi-annual reports by designated firms
cases in which notice of substantial changes must be given
exemption from reporting, notice and wind-down obligations, with attached rules
II, C (Bankwet art. 9c, derde lid via 9q)
amount of administrative fines for cash-transport violations
p: The government may set bank tariffs and customer conditions for cash use by general administrative order, including zero tariffs, with no parliamentary approval step specified.
DNB may order a firm to postpone a substantial change for up to 26 weeks where it deems this necessary for continuity, subject to a fixed time limit and appeal rights.

parties: Wants a full overview of lower regulation and parliamentary involvement via voorhang or nahang procedures, and a planning schedule for when the Chamber is consulted.
These members believe access to cash must be properly arranged for everyone in the Netherlands.
Deze leden vinden ook dat de toegang tot contant geld goed geregeld moet zijn voor iedereen in Nederland.
Asks why the free-of-charge tariff is left to an AMvB rather than the statute, considers an amendment, and wants to see the AMvB before plenary debate.
The NSC members ask why the zero tariff for withdrawing and depositing cash is regulated in an AMvB and not in the statute itself.
De leden van de NSC-fractie vragen waarom het nultarief voor het opnemen en storten van contant geld in een AMvB wordt geregeld en niet in de wet zelf.
Argues that a user-number threshold alone is disproportionate for innovative banks and proposes a hybrid model with balance-sheet criteria.
These members therefore ask whether the government realises that using a user threshold as the sole criterion leads to a disproportionate financial burden for innovative banks.

Deze leden vragen zich hierom af of de regering zich bewust is dat het hanteren van een gebruikersdrempel als enige criterium leidt tot een disproportionele financiële belasting voor innovatieve banken.
Asks how the Raad van State's concern about cartel formation and unfair cost sharing is enforced and whether DNB or ACM should supervise tariffs.
The GroenLinks-PvdA members note that the Council of State sees a risk of cartel formation if only the large banks control the service at Geldmaat.
De leden van de GroenLinks-PvdA-fractie constateren dat de Raad van State een risico ziet op kartelvorming wanneer alleen de grote banken de dienst uit maken bij Geldmaat.
Asks how the AMvB on infrastructure, tariffs and use rules will be filled in, who will be involved and when it will be sent to the Chamber, and asks for an evaluation clause.
How will this AMvB be further elaborated, who will be involved, and when will it be sent to the Chamber?
Hoe zal deze AMvB nader worden ingevuld, wie worden daarbij betrokken en wanneer wordt deze naar de Kamer gestuurd?
Questions unequal access depending on bank, asks whether public organisation of the infrastructure was considered, and wants a clear overview of accessibility standards.
Does this therefore mean unequal access to the cash base infrastructure, depending on which bank one holds an account with?
Is er hierdoor dus sprake van ongelijke toegang tot de chartale basisinfrastructuur, afhankelijk bij welke bank men rekeninghouder is?
Stresses that the real problem is digital inclusion and asks about the choice of a three-million-account threshold and possible transition periods.
Asks what safeguards protect vulnerable groups and small entrepreneurs dependent on cash while no statutory acceptance obligation exists.
The DENK members ask the government what safeguards currently exist for vulnerable groups that depend heavily on cash.
De leden van de DENK-fractie vragen de regering welke waarborgen er op dit moment bestaan voor kwetsbare groepen die in sterke mate afhankelijk zijn van contant geld.
Supports the bill but asks whether further legislation should secure ATM availability and why the threshold and balance-sheet criteria were not used.
Does the government consider it desirable for additional legislation to be introduced to increase the availability of ATMs?
Acht de regering het wenselijk dat er aanvullende wetgeving komt om de beschikbaarheid van geldautomaten te verhogen?
Supports a cash acceptance obligation and asks whether it would have been better handled in a regular legislative process with advisory consultation.

Is the government of the view that it would have been better to implement this acceptance obligation in a regular legislative process, so that implementation tests and a Council of State advice could have been consulted?

Is de regering van mening dat het beter was geweest om deze acceptatieplicht in een regulier wetgevingsproces te implementeren, zodat ook uitvoeringstoetsen en een Raad van State-advies geraadpleegd hadden kunnen worden?

v.summary: The Raad van State's advisory division advised on the Wet chartaal betalingsverkeer, raising competition-law concerns about mandated cooperation among large banks, the proportionality of the storage obligation for smaller banks, and the unclear nature of DNB's power over notified changes at cash-transport firms. The Minister's nader rapport accepts the need to justify the scheme, narrows the scope of the storage obligation to banks with over 500,000 account holders, and clarifies the DNB procedure and legal protection.
concerns: The Afdeling asks how the mandated cooperation among large banks fits with the EU cartel prohibition and the effet utile rule, and advises consulting the ACM and justifying any restriction.
The Afdeling finds the explanation of the proportionality of the storage obligation for smaller banks insufficient and advises further justification of its financial and business effects.
The Afdeling asks what the nature and effect of DNB's judgment on notified changes at cash-transport firms is, and whether it can be challenged in court, advising clarification.

36800-IIB.s: This is the 2026 budget bill (begrotingsstaat) for the other High Colleges of State, the Governors' cabinets of Aruba, Curaçao and Sint Maarten, and the Electoral Council, setting appropriations in thousands of euros. It contains no delegations of rule-making power and no shifts in power between the executive and checks.
q: Article 1: The budget statement belonging to this act for the year 2026 is established.
Artikel 1 De bij deze wet behorende begrotingsstaat voor het jaar 2026 wordt vastgesteld.

v.summary: The Raad van State's Afdeling advisering made no remarks on the draft 2026 budget bill for the other High Councils of State, the Governors' cabinets and the Electoral Council (IIB) and advised submitting it to the House. The Minister of Finance's nader rapport announces only technical adjustments to several budgets in annexes, with no substantive reply to objections.

36810.s: The bill adds Article 4.12b to the Aanbestedingswet 2012, allowing rules by general administrative order (AMvB) on aanbestedende diensten and special-sector undertakings providing data to authorities, other member states, or the European Commission, to implement EU Regulation 2022/1031 on the International Procurement Instrument. It creates no new rights or obligations for procurement procedures itself.
36810.j: The memorandum justifies the delegation as necessary to implement the EU regulation's data-provision obligations, and limits it to rules on data provision to keep the wetgever's primacy intact.
q: This possibility is limited to further rules on the provision by contracting authorities or special-sector undertakings of data to administrative bodies or other agencies, competent authorities of other member states, or the European Commission.

Deze mogelijkheid is beperkt tot nadere regels omtrent de verstrekking door aanbestedende diensten of speciale-sectorbedrijven van gegevens aan bestuursorganen of andere instanties, bevoegde autoriteiten van andere lidstaten of de Europese Commissie.
d: rules on provision of data by contracting entities to authorities and the European Commission under IIO regulation

parties: Asks how the delegation basis avoids becoming a generic basis for other procurement measures and how parliamentary control is ensured given time pressure.
These members ask how the government prevents the delegation basis from becoming in effect a generic basis for other European procurement measures.
Deze leden vragen hoe de regering voorkomt dat de delegatiegrondslag de facto een generieke grondslag wordt voor andere Europese aanbestedingsmaatregelen.
Asks about the relation to other trade instruments, the scope thresholds, the offensive character of the instrument, and the effects on contracting authorities and European businesses.
Can the government explain in what way this regulation leads to a more offensive trade policy from the European Union?
Kan de regering uitleggen op welke manier deze verordening leidt tot offensievere handelspolitiek vanuit de Europese Unie?
Asks whether the instrument is actually used, with examples, and whether the general administrative order is ready and when it will take effect.
The CDA members ask whether the general administrative order (AMvB) for which this bill creates a basis is already ready.
De leden van de CDA-fractie vragen of de algemene maatregel van bestuur (AMvB) waarvoor in dit wetsvoorstel een grondslag gecreëerd wordt, reeds gereed is.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advised that the proposed delegation basis in the Aanbestedingswet 2012 for implementing EU procurement acts is too broad, violating the primacy of the legislature, and should be limited to what is necessary for the IIO Regulation, with justification for the other sub-parts. The minister's reply states the advice is followed by limiting the delegation to the IIO Regulation and the listed subjects, while noting the matter may be revisited for future EU procurement acts.
concerns: The proposed delegation basis for implementing EU procurement acts is too broad and must be limited to what is necessary for the IIO Regulation, which the government followed.
Covering all future EU procurement acts at a lower level than the law conflicts with the primacy of the legislature; the government restricted the scope to the IIO Regulation.
Parts a, b, c and d are not shown to be necessary for IIO measures, and the government did not fully justify them, though it limited the subject matter.

36900.s: The bill amends the Landbouwkwaliteitswet and the Wet dieren to implement EU Regulation 2024/1143 on geographical indications and quality schemes, updating definitions and references. It adds new powers for the Minister of Agriculture to impose a standalone order on hosting providers, domain registries or registrars to remove or block unlawful content, and allows personal data registers and data exchange between authorities.
36900.j: The memorandum justifies the new powers as necessary to implement articles 42 and 43 of Regulation 2024/1143 and balances them with freedom of expression through subsidiarity, proportionality and a one-week delay allowing judicial protection.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised that the bill's proposal to skip the objection phase (bezwaar) before appeal for a standalone order against unlawful quality designations was insufficiently justified in the explanatory memorandum. The minister reply states the objection procedure was retained, article III was deleted and the memorandum adjusted accordingly.
concerns: Skipping the objection phase deviates from the general system of legal protection under the General Administrative Law Act and required explicit motivation, which was lacking.

36915-M.s: The bill amends the 2026 budget statement (begrotingsstaat) of the Klimaatfonds, the climate fund, through a first supplementary budget (eerste suppletoire begroting). It changes expenditure and commitments across climate policy articles such as energy infrastructure, industry sustainability and the built environment, with no explanatory memorandum provided.
